newsitem.title: CHINA: China to spend 120 bln yuan on state firms by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China to spend 120 bln yuan on state firms by 2000.

text.p: China will spend 120 billion yuan ($14.5 billion) over the next three years to reform its ailing state-owned enterprises and write off their bad debts, the International Business Daily said on Saturday.
"This huge amount of funds will mainly be used towards writing off the bad debts of the liabilities of state-owned enterprises," the newspaper said.
The funds would also be used to promote bankruptcies and mergers of state firms, and would complement recent policies to promote such activities, it said.
"Experts predict that the merging and bankruptcy of state firms will make breakthrough developments in the near future," the newspaper said but gave no details.
China has designated 110 pilot cities in which bankruptcies and mergers of state firms can take place.
Beijing has said that reform of the lumbering state sector, with about 70 percent of enterprises making losses or hopelessly in the red, is a priority in 1997.
